scope: Datasets admissible for the Omics2PK five-objective validation (H1-H5). A published article is not by itself an exploitable dataset.

access_policy.rule: Only data effectively retrievable without an authorization request or a collaboration agreement may enter a confirmatory analysis.
access_policy.open_public: Retrievable by URL with no account. Admissible for confirmatory analysis.
access_policy.public_registered: Retrievable by anyone who creates an account and satisfies a gate they can satisfy unilaterally (accepting data-use terms, or a platform certification quiz). No committee reviews the request and no author is contacted. Admissible for confirmatory analysis since the ruling of 2026-11-07, but every entry must declare its access_requirement and the evidence for its type; a committee-reviewed gate belongs to governed_application.
access_policy.author_request: Requires contacting an author. NOT admissible in this phase.
access_policy.governed_application: Requires an ethics/registry committee decision. NOT admissible in this phase.
access_policy.unavailable: No individual-level data released in any form.
forbidden_practices: reconstructing individual rows from published means, figures or ranges
presenting simulated values as biological results
merging unrelated cohorts into a pseudo-subject
counting two drugs measured in the same donors as two independent biological cohorts
access_policy.gate_rule: Admissibility is decided by the access_requirement type, never by the tier name alone. Self-service gates (none, self_sign, certified_user) are admissible; managed_act is not.

status_definitions.ACQUIRED: Source bytes in hand with a recorded SHA-256; identity/endpoint qualification not yet asserted.
status_definitions.QUALIFIED: Acquired AND the biological unit, endpoint, matrix, timing and omics identity have been checked against a named objective.
status_definitions.PARTIAL: Some qualification requirements met; a named requirement is still open.
status_definitions.ABSTAIN: Cannot be used in this phase; reason recorded.

endpoint_classes.pk_clinical: A pharmacokinetic observation in a treated human (concentration, AUC, CL/F).
endpoint_classes.functional_in_vitro: An enzyme activity or intrinsic clearance measured in tissue/microsomes. NOT human PK.
endpoint_classes.pd_cell_line: A cell-line drug-response endpoint. Neither PK nor human PD.
endpoint_classes.biomarker_only: Molecular ratios with a genotype reference but no drug exposure measurement.

verification_legend.verified_this_session: true = the stated provenance facts were checked on 2026-11-07 by retrieving the source and/or recomputing the checksum. false = inherited from a prior repository document and NOT re-verified here.

datasets.label: ARIANA metoprolol n=47
datasets.citation: Saromba JA, Kurt B, Antwerpen A, Rex K, Giacin A, Bornemann J, Aygar K, Mertens M, Mueller-Wieland D, Dahl E, Marx N, Kahles F, Wozniak J, Neiss J, Krzoska D, Stingl JC, Mueller JP, Just KS. Front Pharmacol. 2026 May 29;17:1812007.
datasets.data_availability_statement: Original data were uploaded to a repository accessible under the following link: https://github.com/katjajust/Solandine-Metoprolol-Correlations
datasets.sampling_time: fasting pre-dose trough; absolute clock time and time since last dose NOT documented in the source

omics_layers.identification_quality: solanidine and 4-OH-solanidine quantified; SSDA semi-quantitative, no authentic analytical standard

datasets.genotypes: CYP2D6 SNP panel with copy number; activity score derived (source supplementary S2)
datasets.comedication: CYP2D6 substrate/inhibitor list recorded (source supplementary S3)
datasets.dose_regimen: metoprolol twice daily in equal doses; 23 patients at 95 mg/day and 24 at 190 mg/day
datasets.formulation: NOT documented in the source. Succinate extended-release inferred from the 47.5/95/190 mg German strengths; immediate-release tartrate retained as a sensitivity analysis. Formulation must not be chosen on observed MAE.
datasets.verification_method: Downloaded from the repository named in the data availability statement; SHA-256 recomputed and found identical to the file already used in the local ARIANA analysis.
caveats: One concentration per patient. MAP-Bayesian estimation conditioned on that concentration and then predicting it is circular (measured optimism factor 3.6) and is excluded by construction.

One observation per subject does not make a nonlinear mixed-effects model impossible, but it leaves between-subject variability and residual error not separately identifiable, and it cannot support estimation of individual PK parameters from ARIANA alone. No NLME variability claim is made from this cohort.
The OH-metoprolol/metoprolol metabolic ratio is present in the source but shares its denominator with the target concentration. It may be used ONLY as a validation target, never as a predictor.

The source publication's own primary result is the correlation between solanidine-derived and metoprolol-derived metabolic ratios. Reproducing it is a positive control on the implementation, NOT a new finding of this project.
Single centre, single laboratory, single assay.

prior_analysis_exposure.implication: This cohort has already been analysed repeatedly under earlier internal versions, with model choices made while results were visible. Freezing the protocol prevents further result-guided decisions; it cannot retroactively make this an independent confirmatory validation. Every ARIANA conclusion is reported as an exploratory re-analysis.

prespecification.frozen_in_v1_0_0: arm definitions, the primary contrast and its loss, the loss hierarchy and reversal rule, the CV scheme, influence reporting, the prohibited predictor, the MAP-BE exclusion, and the 10 percent exploratory success threshold.
prespecification.operationalised_at_analysis_time: log-target fitting with back-transformation, penalty grids, feature encodings, bootstrap count.

primary_contrast.definition: Ridge M3 (clinical+PGx+omic) versus Ridge M1 (clinical+PGx), MAE
primary_contrast.criterion: at least 10 percent relative MAE improvement with a descriptive interval excluding zero; observed 32.1 percent

secondary_target_dose_weighted.note: Prespecified secondary. Post-hoc switching between targets is prohibited.

key_secondary_observation.corrected_claim: No additional benefit from pharmacogenetics was DETECTED once the omic ratios were included. The earlier phrasing, that the omic substitutes for the genotype, is withdrawn: every PGx contrast has an interval covering zero, and not detected is not absent.
decomposition_findings: The comedication flag contributes essentially nothing: added to clinical it gives -0.45 [-1.87, +0.98] Ridge, -0.18 [-1.58, +1.22] Elastic Net, -0.42 [-1.80, +0.52] XGBoost, and a 10 percent benefit is excluded in all three. On top of the omic, likewise excluded in all three. XGBoost never used the variable at all: the contrast is exactly 0.00 [0.00, 0.00], because at depth 1-2 with the omic present the binary flag was never chosen as a split.

Whatever small signal the bundled block carried came from the activity score, not the comedication flag: genotype alone gives -2.14 [-5.67, +1.51] Ridge and -3.09 [-7.12, +0.97] Elastic Net, close to the bundled -2.83 and -2.48.

The genotype's own contribution over clinical is INCONCLUSIVE for the linear models: not detected, but the intervals reach about -10 to -13 percent relative, so a benefit of the prespecified size cannot be ruled out at n=47.

Adding the genotype on top of the omic is NOT_SUPPORTED at the frozen margin in all three families: +1.95 [-1.07, +4.96] Ridge, +1.13 [-1.13, +3.25] Elastic Net, +0.84 [-0.25, +1.97] XGBoost. Not detected AND a 10 percent benefit is incompatible with every interval. This is the one genuinely negative statement in the decomposition.
key_secondary_observation.jarmusch_parallel_withdrawn: The earlier claim of two public cohorts with the same ordering does not hold. Jarmusch's functional probe is a prior administered-probe PK measurement of the same drug, not an independent omic biomarker, and its panels and sample sizes differ. Jarmusch is a separate negative H1 test on untargeted metabolomics and corroborates nothing here.
key_secondary_observation.status: secondary and exploratory within the H1 family; Holm adjustment required

influence.reading: The gain is heavily concentrated: five of 47 patients carry about three quarters of it, and that is reported next to the headline. It is nevertheless positive in all four endpoint quartiles and 34 of 47 patients improve individually, which distinguishes it from a pure outlier artefact. Absolute errors scale with concentration over a 7 to 572 ng/mL range, which is why the log and trimmed losses are mandatory co-criteria; both agree.

executed_h1_result.non_circularity: The predictor is a solanidine-derived ratio from a dietary precursor; the target is the metoprolol concentration. They share no analyte and no denominator. The lnMR OH-metoprolol/metoprolol column, which does share a denominator with the target, is absent from every arm and a test enforces it.
limitations: Exploratory only: prior analysis exposure caps the claim.
No public replication cohort exists for this axis, so it cannot be upgraded.

H5 showed the marker's subject ranking changes with sampling time, and ARIANA documents neither absolute sampling time nor time since last meal. This result therefore rests on the unverifiable assumption that ARIANA's samples sit in the informative regime.
Gain concentrated in five of 47 patients.
n=47, single centre, single laboratory, single assay.
One primary contrast unadjusted; every other contrast requires Holm adjustment.

sub_statuses.genotype_alone_over_clinical: INCONCLUSIVE for Ridge and Elastic Net; NOT_SUPPORTED at the margin for XGBoost
sub_statuses.comedication_alone_over_clinical: NOT_SUPPORTED at the margin in all three families
sub_statuses.genotype_on_top_of_omic: NOT_SUPPORTED at the margin in all three families
sub_statuses.comedication_on_top_of_omic: NOT_SUPPORTED at the margin in all three families

executed_h1_result.what_follows: Two distinct H2 experiments. First, does NetPK SELECT better: same model, same number of variables, NetPK selection against SHAP, Elastic Net, nested univariate, repeated random panel, a deliberately wrong mechanistic panel, and no selection. Second, does mechanistic INTEGRATION then help: identical NetPK variables, statistical integration against parameterisation as an enzyme-activity score feeding a PopPK structure. Separating them isolates the value of the selection from the value of the borrowed pharmacological coefficients. Throughout, verify the selection is actually produced by the algorithm and not written into the code after inspecting results.

revision.reason: External review; see the document revision log.

executed_h1_result.status_assignment_rule: Two distinct questions. Was an effect DETECTED: does the interval exclude zero. Can a benefit of the PRESPECIFIED size be EXCLUDED: is the most favourable value in the interval short of -10 percent. Only the second licenses NOT_SUPPORTED; failing both is INCONCLUSIVE. Protocol section 10 forbids reading a zero-crossing interval as evidence of equivalence.
executed_h1_result.why_ariana_cannot_carry_h2: ARIANA has exactly two candidate omic variables. It demonstrates that those two carry predictive information; it is not a demanding test of selection. Choosing 2 of 2 is not selection, and no selector can distinguish itself on a panel that size, so running the H2 comparator set on ARIANA alone would produce a near-tie by construction. H2 needs the wide panels: HLC, EPA, Wegler and the public metabolomic sets, whose endpoints are functional in vitro and are therefore reported as the functional analogue of H2, never in the same effect column as a clinical PK result.

datasets.label: Mueller phenotyping cocktail n=20 (2024 study)
datasets.citation: Mueller JP, Saromba J, Ziegler P, Tremmel R, Rengelshausen J, Schaeffeler E, Just KS, Schwab M, Kraus T, Stingl JC. Clin Pharmacol Ther. 2024 Feb;115(2):309-317.
datasets.design: phenotyping cocktail in healthy volunteers; 12.5 mg oral metoprolol; 15 plasma sampling points over 24 h; solanidine, 4-OH-solanidine and SSDA by LC-MS; all participants CYP2D6 genotyped

endpoint.name: AUC metabolic ratio alpha-OH-metoprolol/metoprolol and solanidine-derived ratios

datasets.abstain_reason: No individual-level data released. Europe PMC core record reports hasData=N, hasSuppl=N, no PMCID; the publisher page returns HTTP 403. Published aggregate values must not be converted into reconstructed individual rows.
datasets.verification_method: Europe PMC REST core record for DOI 10.1002/cpt.3106 retrieved and inspected; publisher full text attempted and refused.
datasets.consequence: WITHDRAWN in registry 1.2.0. This entry previously concluded that no public dataset could test within-subject temporal stability of the solanidine ratios. That conclusion was wrong: see muller_potato_meal_20, a different study by the same first author which releases individual time-course data openly. This 2024 cocktail study itself remains ABSTAIN.

datasets.label: Mueller standardized potato meal n=20 (2026 study)
datasets.citation: Mueller JP, Friske D, Hasoumi M, Miller B, Saromba J, Tupiec J, Koczera P, Laurentius T, Clavel T, Stingl JC, Just KS. Solanidine metabolic ratios for CYP2D6 phenotyping after a standardized potato meal. Front Pharmacol. 2026 Oct 2;17:1886427.
datasets.citation_verified_via: Crossref API, 2026-11-07: title, journal, volume 17, article 1886427, published 2026-10-02, 11 authors.
datasets.access_note: Public GitHub repository, retrievable by URL with no account.
datasets.redistribution_note: No licence file is present in the source repository, so redistribution rights are unstated. The workbook is therefore NOT committed; acquisition is by script with a checksum, exactly as for ARIANA.
datasets.design: Single standardized potato meal, no drug administered. 9 plasma sampling points per participant at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 29 hours.

omics_layers.identification_quality: Solanidine and 4-OH-solanidine are reported in concentration units with a stated limit of quantification. SSDA is reported in raw counts and is therefore SEMI-QUANTITATIVE, the same analytical weakness recorded for ARIANA.
omics_layers.completeness: 180 of 180 cells present for each of the three analytes; no missing values

loq_imputation.method_stated_in_source: Values below the limit of quantification were imputed as half the lower limit of quantification for solanidine (0.01 ng/ml) and 4-OH-solanidine (0.02 ng/ml), or as the lowest measured value for SSDA.
loq_imputation.critical_limitation: Participant 1, the cohort's only poor metaboliser (*4/*4x2, activity score 0), is below the limit of quantification at ALL 9 timepoints for BOTH metabolites. The metabolic ratio is therefore entirely imputed for the one subject the marker most needs to identify. Any discriminative performance at the poor-metaboliser end rests on imputed floor values and must be reported as such.
loq_imputation.extraction_method: Imputed cells carry no data flag; they are distinguishable only by bold font. Reading them requires openpyxl font inspection, not a plain value read, so any pandas-only pipeline would silently treat imputed floors as measurements.

genotypes.activity_score_convention_conflict: This cohort scores *41 as 0.25, the post-2021 CPIC convention. The Rudesheim 2020 activity-score-to-relative-activity mapping used by the mechanistic module is built on the grid (0, 0.5, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3) and predates that change. Activity scores are therefore NOT directly comparable between this cohort and ARIANA, and the mapping must not be applied across them without an explicit convention alignment. This is a prespecified H5 item, not a correction to be made silently.
genotypes.phenotype_distribution_verified_by: scripts/qualify_muller2026_potato_meal_source.py, which recounted the participant sheet and corrected an earlier hand-entered 9/9 split.

covariates.food_exposure_flag: 'Fasted on potato products for 3 days': 15 participants yes, 5 no. This makes a food effect directly testable.

additional_source_sheets.content: The meal itself was assayed: 4 potato fritter aliquots with alpha-chaconine, alpha-solanine and solanidine content, plus mean and standard deviation. The precursor dose is therefore quantified, which permits a precursor-normalised biomarker analysis.
Two stool samples incubated with alpha-solanine or alpha-chaconine under active versus inactivated microbial community, in triplicate. Solanidine is formed only with an active community.
additional_source_sheets.mechanistic_consequence: Solanidine supply is gut-microbiota dependent. The biomarker therefore carries a variance source upstream of CYP2D6 that genotype cannot capture, which is a mechanistic argument for why a measured ratio can outperform a genotype estimate AND a reason its reproducibility may be limited. Both directions must be tested.

endpoint.name: solanidine-derived metabolic ratios as CYP2D6 phenotype markers

datasets.qualified_for: H5 only, and specifically the three items previously recorded as ABSTAIN: the sampling-time effect, the food effect, and intra-individual temporal stability of the solanidine ratios. Also the quantified-versus-semi-quantitative comparison, since solanidine is in ng/ml and SSDA in counts.
datasets.cannot_support: H1 and any pharmacokinetic claim. No drug is administered, so there is no PK endpoint and no exposure to predict. This dataset does NOT replicate the ARIANA solanidine-to-exposure association; it can only test whether the marker itself behaves reproducibly.
datasets.independence_limitation: NOT a fully independent replication. Saromba J, Stingl JC and Just KS are authors of both this study and ARIANA, so the cohort shares a research group, laboratory and analytical platform with ARIANA. The participants are different people (20 healthy volunteers versus 47 cardiology patients), so this is a different population measured by the same group, not an independent laboratory. Any agreement between the two must be reported with that limitation stated, since shared method bias would produce agreement as well.
datasets.verification_method: GitHub API confirmed the public repository and its two files on 2026-11-07. The workbook was downloaded and its SHA-256 computed. All four sheets were parsed: participant table (20 rows, complete), plasma concentrations (3 analyte blocks of 20 participants x 9 timepoints, 180/180 cells each, no missing values), glycoalkaloid assay and microbial incubations. Bold-font imputation flags were extracted with openpyxl and counted. Crossref confirmed the citation.
caveats: No drug administered: this is a biomarker reproducibility cohort, never a PK cohort.
n=20 healthy young volunteers (ages 22-27), so results do not transfer to a multimorbid comedicated population without an explicit argument.
Only 1 poor metaboliser and 1 ultrarapid metaboliser, and the poor metaboliser is entirely below the limit of quantification. The extremes of the phenotype range are represented by one subject each.
SSDA is in counts, so between-cohort absolute comparison is not meaningful.
Shares authors, laboratory and platform with ARIANA.

executed_h5_result.headline: The activity-score association is detected only in the late (29 h) sample, in both censoring scenarios. No early-window timepoint reaches significance after correction over the primary family of 18 comparisons. This does NOT establish that the marker is uninformative early: see detectability.

sampling_time_effect.early_window_0_to_5h: OH-solanidine rho -0.14 to +0.28, all p >= 0.32; SSDA rho +0.23 to +0.47, all p >= 0.066. None survives correction.
sampling_time_effect.reproducible_but_not_valid: Early timepoints agree strongly with each other (rank agreement with the 3 h ranking +0.46 to +0.90 for OH-solanidine, +0.75 to +0.96 for SSDA) while agreeing poorly with the informative 29 h ranking (+0.00 to +0.55 and +0.43 to +0.75). A reproducibility study confined to the early window would have been falsely reassuring.
sampling_time_effect.status_change: Downgraded from SUPPORTED in revision 1.1 and held there in 1.2. The measured rank instability across timepoints is robust. The association-strength comparison between windows is not established: early-window intervals reach +0.69 and +0.79 and overlap the 29 h estimates.

multiplicity.survival: At the primary family all four 29 h tests survive (OH-solanidine p 0.00013 all values and 0.00068 censored; SSDA p 0.00044 and 0.00218). At the conservative count only SSDA-censored fails.

imputation_artefact.status: SUPPORTED, but the attribution is corrected
imputation_artefact.original_claim_was_wrong: The first version attributed the ICC fall from 0.942 to 0.400 to below-LOQ imputation.
imputation_artefact.attribution_analysis: Restricting both arms to a common subject set and removing the fixed time effect: OH-solanidine 0.393 all values versus 0.430 censored on 17 common subjects, so the censoring-only delta is -0.037; SSDA 0.779 versus 0.798 on 18 common subjects, delta -0.020. Censoring raises the ICC slightly rather than lowering it.
imputation_artefact.real_mechanism: Three subjects wholly pinned at the imputed floor, participant 1 among them, inflate between-subject variance when included. Excluding them from BOTH arms leaves OH-solanidine at ICC 0.35-0.43.
imputation_artefact.time_effect: Removing the fixed time effect raises the ICC in every cell (0.349 to 0.393; 0.705 to 0.779), confirming the postprandial trajectory inflated the within-subject term.
imputation_artefact.what_still_stands: A value-only pipeline would report ICC 0.942 for OH-solanidine when a comparable-population estimate is near 0.4. A reliability statistic computed over a population containing subjects pinned at an assay floor is not a reliability statistic.

quantified_vs_semiquantitative.finding: The counts-based SSDA is more robust than the ng/ml OH-solanidine on every stability measure: ICC after censoring 0.754 vs 0.400, Kendall W 0.83 vs 0.66, rank agreement with the informative timepoint, and sign consistency across times.
quantified_vs_semiquantitative.do_not_overstate: At the informative timepoint OH-solanidine has the marginally stronger association in both cohorts (0.71 vs 0.66 in Muller at 29 h; 0.489 vs 0.405 in ARIANA). Neither marker dominates: OH-solanidine is slightly more associated when sampling time is controlled, SSDA degrades less when it is not.
quantified_vs_semiquantitative.strengthened_in_revision_1_1: The marker difference now survives a common subject set and removal of the fixed time effect in all four cells: SSDA 0.705-0.798 against OH-solanidine 0.349-0.430. It is not an artefact of differing subject sets or of the postprandial trend.

food_effect.finding: Fasted subjects show lower ratios in every scenario, but all descriptive 95% intervals cover zero with only 5 non-fasted subjects. Reported as inconclusive, explicitly NOT as evidence of no food effect.
food_effect.confounding: The fasting flag and the sampling-time effect are not separable here; both bear on recent dietary precursor supply.

poor_metaboliser_discrimination.reason: The only poor metaboliser is below the limit of quantification at all 9 timepoints for both metabolites.

between_day_reproducibility.reason: Nine samples follow a single meal. Within-occasion dispersion is not between-day reproducibility.

ariana_direction_consistency.reading: Same sign, overlapping intervals and the same ordering between markers, but for the late sample only. Weaker than it looks: the cohorts share authors, laboratory and platform, so shared method bias would produce this agreement.

executed_h5_result.consequence_for_h1: ARIANA sampled at trough but documents neither absolute sampling time nor time since the last meal. Its exposure-prediction result therefore rests on the unverifiable assumption that its samples sit in the informative regime. This must be stated as a limitation of the H1 result rather than discovered afterwards.

revision.reason: Two final statistical precisions; see the document change log.

prespecification.frozen_in_protocol_v1_0_0: H5 objectives and criterion families: intra-individual coefficients of variation, ranking stability, robustness to matrix and time, 95 percent intervals, quantified versus semi-quantitative identification.
prespecification.operationalised_at_analysis_time: Spearman rather than Pearson, the intraclass correlation, Kendall W, the reference times.
prespecification.post_hoc_choice_declared: The 3 h reference was fixed before any run. The 29 h reference was added after the first run showed 29 h to be informative, so statistics anchored on 29 h are exploratory.
prespecification.not_selective: All nine timepoints computed and reported; none dropped.

detectability.this_is_not_an_upper_bound: It is the correlation at which the test would have 80 percent power. A non-significant result does NOT imply the true correlation lies below it.

genuine_compatibility_bounds.consequence: These overlap the 29 h estimates (+0.709 and +0.658), so this design does not separate the early window from the late sample on association strength. The only admissible statement is that early-window associations are not established with the available precision.

detectability.prohibited_inference: Treating a difference in significance as significance of a difference.

marker_difference_on_exact_intersection.why: The per-marker attribution uses each marker's own retained subjects (17 and 18), so a difference between markers was partly a difference of population.
marker_difference_on_exact_intersection.excluded_subjects_are: the floor-pinned subjects, so neither marker is at the assay floor in this comparison
marker_difference_on_exact_intersection.bootstrap: 2000 resamples, subjects as the independent unit; timepoints within a subject are not resampled.
marker_difference_on_exact_intersection.conclusion: The semi-quantitative counts-based analyte is the more reliable of the two. This survives population matching, removal of the postprandial trend, and explicit uncertainty quantification. It is the strongest single result of the H5 analysis.

datasets.h1_functional_analogue_note: Incremental value of CYP transcript over a clinical baseline is measurable here, but on microsomal enzyme activity. It is the functional analogue of H1 and must never be reported as H1, which is defined on clinical pharmacokinetics.
datasets.qualified_for: H3/H4/H5 directly, plus the functional analogue of H1, on an in vitro endpoint only. Confirmatory-admissible since the 2026-11-07 gate ruling. It can never satisfy the H1 criterion, which is stated on clinical PK.
datasets.verification_method: All four local archive SHA-256 values recomputed on 2026-11-07 and found identical to those recorded in docs/HLC_ORIGINAL_400_LIVER_CYP_RNA_GENOTYPE_RESULTS_20261018.md. The access gate and the four source entity IDs were independently re-verified the same day against the Synapse public REST API without authentication.
caveats: No matched quantitative CYP protein, so the RNA -> protein -> activity chain cannot be completed in this cohort.
Body weight is missing for most donors and must not be imputed as if observed.
Source terms prohibit redistribution and any attempt to identify donors; only aggregates may be committed.
Absolute MAE magnitudes are in source assay units and should be reported as within-endpoint relative changes.

access_requirement.evidence: Unauthenticated GET /repo/v1/entity/syn4629/accessRequirement on 2026-11-07 returned exactly one requirement, id 9604913, concreteType SelfSignAccessRequirement, accessType DOWNLOAD, subject syn4499, with isCertifiedUserRequired=false and isValidatedProfileRequired=false. The ACL at benefactor syn4492 grants READ+DOWNLOAD to principal 273948 (AUTHENTICATED_USERS) and READ only to 273949 (PUBLIC), confirming that an account plus the self-signed terms is the whole of the gate.
access_requirement.anonymous_download_refusal: An unauthenticated presigned-URL request returns HTTP 403 with reason 'There are unmet access requirements that must be met to read content in the requested container.' Entity metadata is readable anonymously; the file bytes are not.

retrieval.verification_method: Unauthenticated POST /repo/v1/entity/children on parent syn4499 returned exactly these four file entities; their names match the four local archives one to one.

reacquisition_confirmation.route: Owner downloaded the whole syn4499 folder through the self-signed gate as a single 136114988-byte bundle containing the four entity archives plus Synapse's own manifest.csv.

datasets.omic_crosswalk_status: RESOLVED, with a documented preprocessing deviation. The authors' input GNPS_quant.csv is absent from their GitHub repository, but the GNPS processed output qiime2_output/qiime2_table.qza is held locally: an HDF5 BIOM with 6349 unique MS1 features across 1198 analytical sample IDs. Filtering MS_SampleType=sample, blood_plasma, day 1, time 0 min yields 13 distinct biological subjects with predose plasma MS1, each matched to day-1 targeted midazolam oral CL/F, CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 calls, sex and measured weight. 12 of the 13 also have day-9 CL/F. Analytical replicates share patient/day/time and were verified consistent before collapsing to one observation per person-day; replicate rows are never counted as independent people.
datasets.corrects: Two successive corrections. Registry 1.2.0 withdrew the claim that ARIANA was the only public cohort with PK, omics and PGx, since Jarmusch has PK and PGx matched per individual. Registry 1.3.0 further withdraws the statement that the omic crosswalk was unresolved: it was reconstructed from the GNPS processed output and the H1 comparison has been run, with a negative result.
datasets.omic_identification_caveat: The qza is a GNPS/QIIME2 processed output, not the authors' input table. Its peak areas are not verified numerically identical to GNPS_quant.csv. Most ions are unidentified or isobaric, and a GNPS annotation is not a standard-confirmed structure, so this cohort cannot carry a named-biomarker claim.

executed_h1_result.design: Leave-one-person-out, Ridge alpha=1 predicting log midazolam oral CL/F. Arms: sex+weight; + CYP3A4/CYP3A5 one-hot encoded on training subjects only; + 2 train-only unsupervised principal components of the day-1 time-0 MS1 vectors.
executed_h1_result.units_caveat: Source CL/F physical units are not securely verified; MAE values are in the source's numeric scale and are comparable only within a row.

day1.shuffled_negative_controls: 25 person-to-metabolome shuffles had median augmented MAE 8.0924, and all 25 beat the true-pairing omic model. Random pairings outperformed the real one.

day9.direction: omics slightly worse, interval covers zero
day9.shuffled_negative_controls: 25 shuffles had median augmented MAE 4.6313, with 13 of 25 at or below the real model.

executed_h1_result.interpretation: A genuine paired human omic-to-clinical-PK comparison in which untargeted metabolomics did NOT improve on measured CYP3A4/CYP3A5 variants, on either day. This is a real negative result for H1 and is retained as such. It does not establish that mechanism-targeted metabolite scores cannot help elsewhere: 6349 features projected onto 2 global principal components in n=12-13 is a weak, non-specific covariate, which is a plausible reason for the failure independent of the biology.
executed_h1_result.why_the_negative_result_is_conservative: The GNPS/MZmine feature alignment was computed across the complete assay set BEFORE the leave-one-out split, so the feature universe is transductively informed by the held-out samples. That deviation can only favour the omic arm. The omic arm lost anyway, which makes the negative finding stronger rather than weaker.
executed_h1_result.why_this_does_not_qualify_for_h1: The frozen protocol requires preprocessing inside training folds only. The feature universe here was built once across all samples, so this analysis cannot serve as a qualifying H1 test however informative it is. The entry stays ACQUIRED, which keeps it out of h1_eligible_datasets.

datasets.one_cohort_not_several: Four drug probes (midazolam, caffeine, omeprazole and metabolites) were measured in the SAME 14 donors. These are one biological cohort, never several independent cohorts, and day 1 versus day 9 in the same person are paired occasions, not independent subjects.

amendments.ruling: public_registered is confirmatory-admissible when, and only when, the download gate is one the requester satisfies unilaterally.
amendments.rationale: The public-only rule forbids data whose access needs an authorization request or a collaboration. A Synapse SelfSignAccessRequirement is neither: acceptance of the data-use terms grants access by itself, nobody reviews or decides, and no author is contacted. A ManagedACTAccessRequirement is a committee decision and stays excluded.
amendments.why_that_matters: The ruling was recorded before any HLC model was fitted under this protocol, so it cannot have been influenced by an observed result. No HLC performance figure existed under this protocol at the time of the ruling.
amendments.does_not_change: HLC's endpoint remains functional_in_vitro. It is admissible for H3/H4/H5 and the functional analogue of H1. It still cannot satisfy H1, and ARIANA remains the only H1-eligible dataset.

amendments.ruling: Erratum. Four provenance and status corrections following external review.
amendments.requested_by: repository owner, relaying an external review
corrections: E1: a second Mueller study was missed. The Phase 1 audit checked the 2024 phenotyping cocktail (doi 10.1002/cpt.3106) and concluded no public solanidine time-course data existed. A different study by the same first author, doi 10.3389/fphar.2026.1886427, releases individual data openly. Registered as muller_potato_meal_20.

E2: the claim that ARIANA is the only public dataset with matched clinical PK, omics and pharmacogenetics was wrong. Jarmusch releases an individual pharmacogenomic table for 14 participants together with midazolam CL/F. The correct claim is narrower and is now stated on named, quantified biomarkers.

E3: ARIANA conclusions are an exploratory re-analysis of a cohort this project has already analysed repeatedly, not an independent confirmatory validation. Recorded as prior_analysis_exposure on the entry.

E4: 'an NLME likelihood is not identifiable from a single observation per subject' was too strong. One observation per subject does not make every NLME model impossible; it makes between-subject and residual variability not separately identifiable.
amendments.why_that_matters: The H5 analysis items that muller_potato_meal_20 makes testable were frozen in protocol v1.0.0 before this dataset was known to exist, which is verifiable from the v1.0.0 commit. No criterion was written or altered with this data in view.
amendments.does_not_change: H1 remains unreplicable on public data: the new Mueller study administers no drug, so it carries no pharmacokinetic endpoint. ARIANA remains the only H1-eligible dataset.

amendments.ruling: Correction to erratum item E2. The Jarmusch omic-to-PK crosswalk is NOT unresolved: it was reconstructed from the GNPS processed output and the H1 comparison has already been executed, with a negative result.
amendments.requested_by: repository owner, relaying an external review
corrections: E2 said the Jarmusch subject crosswalk was unresolved. Half right: the authors' own input GNPS_quant.csv is indeed absent from their repository, but the GNPS *processed output* qiime2_output/qiime2_table.qza (6349 MS1 features x 1198 analytical sample IDs) is in hand, and filtering to plasma / day 1 / time 0 min yields 13 matched biological subjects with predose MS1, day-1 midazolam CL/F and CYP3A4/CYP3A5 calls. Jarmusch is therefore a second public test of H1, not a pending one.

The external review described the matched set as 10 volunteers and the results as 'some numerical improvements whose intervals cover zero'. Both are wrong against the repository's own record: the matched set is 13 on day 1 and 12 on day 9, and the omic arm was WORSE than the pharmacogenetic baseline on both days, with the day-1 interval excluding zero on the harmful side.
amendments.why_that_matters: This amendment describes a run that already happened under an earlier internal version, so it is a corrected description of an existing result, not a new prespecification. The result is reported as exploratory and its pipeline deviation from the frozen protocol is recorded explicitly.
amendments.does_not_change: ARIANA remains the only dataset QUALIFIED for H1 and so the only entry in h1_eligible_datasets. Jarmusch gains H1 as a supported objective but stays ACQUIRED, because its feature universe was built across all samples before fold splitting, which the frozen protocol does not permit for a qualifying analysis.

amendments.ruling: Records the executed H5 result on muller_potato_meal_20. No criterion changed.
amendments.why_that_matters: This records an outcome, not a rule. The H5 criteria were frozen in protocol v1.0.0 before this dataset was known to exist, so the analysis plan predates the data.

amendments.ruling: Revises the recorded H5 result after external review. One conclusion is reversed.
amendments.requested_by: repository owner, relaying an external review
corrections: The prespecification claim was too strong. Protocol v1.0.0 froze the H5 objectives and criterion families, not the statistics. Spearman, the ICC, Kendall W and the reference times were operationalised at analysis time, and the 29 h reference was chosen AFTER the first run identified 29 h as informative.

REVERSED: the ICC fall from 0.942 to 0.400 was attributed to below-LOQ imputation. On a common subject set with the fixed time effect removed, censoring RAISES the ICC slightly (delta -0.037 for OH-solanidine, -0.020 for SSDA). The headline drop is caused by including three subjects wholly pinned at the imputed floor.

The sampling-time status is downgraded from SUPPORTED to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. At n approximately 19 the minimum detectable Spearman at 80 percent power under Bonferroni correction is 0.76, so the early-window nulls bound any association below that value rather than excluding one.
Multiplicity restated over the correct primary family of 18 comparisons (2 markers x 9 timepoints), not 9.
amendments.does_not_change: The marker-difference conclusion survives and is strengthened: on a common subject set, with and without the time effect removed, SSDA ICC is 0.71-0.80 against 0.35-0.43 for OH-solanidine. Still no pharmacokinetic claim: no drug was administered.

amendments.ruling: Two final statistical precisions on the H5 result. No status changes.
amendments.requested_by: repository owner, relaying an external review
corrections: The 80 percent power correlation of 0.76 was misused as an upper bound. It is the correlation at which the test would have 80 percent power; a non-significant result does not imply the true correlation is below it. The genuine compatibility bounds are the per-timepoint confidence intervals, whose widest early-window upper limits are +0.69 for OH-solanidine and +0.79 for SSDA. Those overlap the 29 h estimates, so the design does not separate the early and late windows on association strength.

The marker ICC comparison used each marker's own retained subjects, 17 against 18, so part of the difference was a difference of population. Recomputed on the exact intersection with a subject bootstrap; the conclusion is strengthened.
amendments.does_not_change: No status changes. The sampling-time item stays PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED and the marker difference stays SUPPORTED, now with an interval.

amendments.why_that_matters: This records an outcome. The primary contrast, its loss, the loss hierarchy, the CV scheme, the influence reporting and the 10 percent success threshold were all frozen in protocol v1.0.0 before the run.

amendments.ruling: Three corrections to the H1 record after external review. One claim withdrawn.
amendments.requested_by: repository owner, relaying an external review
corrections: WITHDRAWN: the claim that the omic substitutes for the genotype. Every contrast involving the PGx block has a 95 percent interval covering zero, including PGx added to clinical alone. The admissible statement is that no additional PGx benefit was DETECTED once the omic ratios were included. Each contrast now also reports whether a benefit of the prespecified size can be excluded, so NOT_SUPPORTED is distinguished from INCONCLUSIVE rather than conflated.

The PGx block bundled the genotype-derived activity score with the comedication flag, so an effect could not be attributed to either. Decomposed into M1a/M1b genotype and comedication alone and M3a/M3b the same on top of the omic.

WITHDRAWN: the parallel with Jarmusch. Jarmusch's functional probe is a prior administered-probe PK measurement of the same drug, close to a direct measurement of the outcome process, not an independent omic biomarker. Its panels, sample sizes and predictor type all differ, so it does not corroborate anything about genotype versus measured function.
amendments.does_not_change: The primary contrast and its result are untouched: Ridge M3 versus M1, delta MAE -16.97, 95 percent [-33.76, -4.69], criterion met at 32.1 percent, both robustness co-criteria agreeing. Only the secondary interpretation is corrected.

amendments.ruling: Register the four public knowledge sources that make the mechanistic selection executable, and record two negative methodological findings established before any endpoint was read.
amendments.requested_by: repository owner, relaying an external review: making the knowledge-graph to ranking to decision chain executable is the priority, because a hard-coded retained set demonstrates a human reading biology rather than an algorithm
corrections: The selection is no longer written into the code. A new module computes the ordering from a downloaded public network, with seeds obtained automatically from the analysed dataset's own column name, from a public pathway annotation, or from a public chemical-gene resource. A test scans the module source and fails if any gene symbol appears in it, and a second test re-derives the decision from its written definition. The protocol's mandatory honesty check is therefore enforced mechanically rather than asserted.

FINDING, before any endpoint was read: a propagation score cannot be given a calibrated significance threshold. An empirical p-value from B resamples cannot fall below 1/(B+1), while a Benjamini-Hochberg threshold over sixteen thousand candidate genes is of order 1e-6, so the first version of the rule could never retain anything. Replacing the p-value with a permutation false-discovery estimator on node counts removes that resolution floor but not the deeper problem: every null that preserves the degree sequence also preserves how many nodes reach a given proximity, so the count ratio is near one wherever the walk is informative. Measured on the real network, the threshold rule retains one or two genes for all ten endpoints, and retains the same number when deliberately given the wrong enzyme.

CONSEQUENCE for the H2 design: the number of variables to keep is not delegated to the network. The module supplies a ranking; the cut is chosen inside training folds only, exactly as a data-driven competitor chooses its own. Every arm then uses the endpoint in the same way and the only difference between arms is where the ordering came from, which is the comparison H2 actually requires.

The probe substrates of eight of the ten enzyme assays are not retrievable from any accessible source: the archive's own readme names only two, the 2008 publication does not describe the assays, and the 2010 publication's substrate list sits in a supplement absent from the open repository with the publisher path returning 404. Naming them from memory would be an unverifiable input, so the substrate-seeded variant runs on the two documented endpoints only and is reported as an illustration of the chain, not as a test.
amendments.does_not_change: No H1 or H5 result. The H1 primary contrast on ARIANA and the H5 result on the potato-meal cohort are untouched; this amendment concerns only how H2 will be conducted and what prior-knowledge resources it may use.

amendments.change: Registers the three annotation references the qualified probe pools depend on: the GEO GPL4372 platform record, NCBI's human gene_info, and the human subset of NCBI gene2accession. They were used before being registered, which is the gap this amendment closes: the pool file carried their checksums but the registry did not carry their provenance, so the project's source of truth for public data did not list what decides the identity of every measured feature. Two roles are added for them, `probe_annotation` and `gene_reference`. None is redistributable by any verified permission and none is committed; the GEO record's URL was re-downloaded and found byte-identical to the local artefact, so the stated URL is the one actually used. A knowledge source still supports no objective.

Two records, neither of which changes any dataset's status. (1) Registers CollecTRI as served by the OmniPath web service, the signed regulatory network the F-series arms are built from. Its licence is composite and was NOT verified, so no redistribution is assumed and the file stays out of the repository; what was verified is that the recorded URL returns a response byte-identical to the local artefact, so the registry carries a reproducible download rather than a reconstructed one. The structural counts the frozen rules depend on are recorded with it, including that 822 of its 64,516 edges have a cytochrome target and are removed before any score is computed. (2) Records the re-verification of the ARIANA workbook on 2026-11-09: the file was absent from local disk, was re-downloaded from its public GitHub repository, and its SHA-256 matched the registered value bit-for-bit. The registered checksum is therefore the checksum of the file the ARIANA runs read. A knowledge source still supports no objective.
